title: Decorators & Closures: Class-Based Decorators & State Retention

slides.title: Class-Based Decorators
slides.prompt: A class can be used as a decorator by implementing the `__init__` method (to receive the function) and the `__call__` method (to act as the wrapper). Class decorators are ideal for maintaining clean state across calls.

slides.title: Storing State in Class Decorators

slides.title: Decorating Instance Methods with Class Decorator
slides.prompt: What issue occurs when using a simple class-based decorator on an instance method of another class?
options: The decorated method loses automatic binding to 'self', causing argument count mismatches
Python raises a SyntaxError at definition time
Class decorators cannot be placed above instance methods
The method is converted into a staticmethod automatically
slides.correctAnswer: The decorated method loses automatic binding to 'self', causing argument count mismatches

slides.title: Class Decorator with Arguments Syntax
slides.prompt: When a class decorator takes arguments (e.g., `@MyDec(arg=1)`), where is `func` passed?
options: To the `__call__` method when the decorator instance is called with `func`
slides.correctAnswer: To the `__call__` method when the decorator instance is called with `func`
